candidates.title: PRT stored player refuses every valid template that already commits to outputs: store_first_epoch_checkpoint asserts the template's tx-buffer root is the empty outputs tree, so it cannot defend a non-genesis template
candidates.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua store_first_epoch_checkpoint, used by prt-demo.lua and by the crisium.lua epoch-0 checkpoint flow)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md table: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'). It stands in for the honest operator: it computes claims.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua:2741-2777 store_first_epoch_checkpoint: `local outputs_frontier = new_outputs_frontier()` (always the empty frontier, prt.lua:2463-2473) then `assert(machine:read_memory(CMIO_TX_BUFFER_ADDRESS, WORD_SIZE) == outputs_root, "template machine has an output history")`; the function takes no outputs frontier or last-output proof argument. crisium.lua:234-237 then requires checkpoints/epoch-0 to exist and to hold the template hash, so there is no other supported way to start epoch 0.
candidates.description: The threat model's valid template is a state whose 'tx buffer holds the outputs Merkle root of every output that the application accepted before it, which at genesis is the root of the empty outputs tree' (section 2), so templates with a non-empty output history are valid templates; the manual documents them too (doc/README.md ~2414: 'For a non-genesis template, use --assert-rolling-template=outputs_merkle_root:<filename>'). The stored PRT player's only way to create the epoch-0 checkpoint hard-codes an empty outputs frontier and aborts with 'template machine has an output history' for any other template. Claims and proofs do not depend on the outputs at all (outputs are opaque guest data, section 4), yet the player refuses to compute any claim. hash_tree.frontier(last_output_proof) exists and could seed the frontier, but store_first_epoch_checkpoint offers no way to pass one, and for claims it is not even needed (the non-stored player just reports an outputs_merkle_root_mismatch anomaly in the same situation).
candidates.trigger: An application deployed (e.g. via DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp, which accepts any templateHash) from a valid template that continues an earlier output history (a migrated application). No adversary needed; the honest operator running the recipe player cannot start, so any claim, including a fabricated final state, wins epoch 0 and every later epoch by default.
candidates.reachability: Reachable with a template built as the manual documents: run the guest so it emits outputs and accepts, store it at the rx-accepted yield (cartesi-machine --assert-rolling-template=outputs_merkle_root:<file> --store=...). Its tx-buffer word is a non-empty-tree root; store_first_epoch_checkpoint asserts.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No: the trigger is a valid template meeting every condition of section 2 (reproducible, pristine uarch, rx-accepted manual yield, tx buffer holding the root of outputs accepted before it); no excluded trigger (not an application that is incorrectly designed, not a non-valid snapshot). 2 Role: the PRT player is Support per the AUDIT.md table; section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator or a tool that computes claims.' 3 High/Medium cases: as support it matches 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'. In the honest-operator role it stands in for, it would violate R4 ('From any reachable state, at the position where it is reached, the honest operator can always compute the claim') on the honest operator's path ('Obtaining its valid template'), which section 8 rates Critical ('violating any rule or obligation ... anywhere on the honest operator's path, is critical'). 4/5 not reached. Claimed: Medium (support). If triage reads doc/README.md:2392 'A template is the genesis of a Cartesi Rollups application' as restricting PRT templates to genesis, the manual contradicts both itself (~2414) and the threat model's valid-template definition; section 8: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.'
candidates.threat_to_goal: Section 1 assumes one honest operator defends the result; with the recipe player as that operator, a valid non-genesis template leaves no honest claim, so any claim settles any final state and outputs (section 8 out-of-scope note: 'If it stopped, any claim could win, a fabricated final state and its outputs included'). Production nodes are out of scope; the defect is in the reference operator implementation.
candidates.evidence: Code reading of prt.lua:2741-2777, 2463-2473, crisium.lua:225-260, prt-epoch.lua:83-97 (the epoch-0 seal check compares outputsMerkleRoot with eth.zero, consistent with DaveConsensus's constructor, so the only blocker is the checkpoint assert). Not run.
candidates.test_idea: Build a template from a bare-metal guest that emits one tx-output automatic yield, writes the matching root (keccak leaf of the output, padded height-63 frontier) to the tx buffer and yields rx-accepted; store it. Call prt.store_first_epoch_checkpoint(template_dir, prt.new_geometry(11), dir) inside pcall; the required behavior is that it succeeds (or accepts a previous outputs frontier/last-output proof) and a stored player can then compute the epoch-0 claim. Exit 1 when it raises 'template machine has an output history'.

not_covered: Dave tournament internals that decide which claim becomes ROOT_WINNER (match/timeout/elimination, inner-tournament propagation): only tournamentStanding, joinTournament/requireFinalState and Commitment.getRootForLastLeaf were read, to confirm the staged state is the authenticated last leaf of the winning commitment.

No on-chain run: stageTournamentResult/acceptStagedTournamentResult/executeOutput were checked by reading only (DaveConsensus.sol, LibMachineValidityProof, LibLeafProof, LibBinaryMerkleTree, LibOutputValidityProof, Application.sol); no gas measurement of staging or executeOutput proofs.

Checked and found consistent (no candidate): machine validity proof constants (iflags_Y 0x308, tohost 0x330, tx buffer 0x60800000, HTIF masks/shifts, accepted reason 1, 59 siblings, keccak(32-byte word) leaves) against this emulator; outputs proof (63 siblings, index range check in merkleRootAfterReplacement, leaf = keccak(output bytes)); executed bitmap keyed by global output index set before the call; executeOutput not gated by foreclosure; roots recorded only at acceptance from the ROOT_WINNER final state; wasInputFinalized/refund/accounts-drive consistency with the last finalized state; the referee model's game-output.lua and wait_for_outputs (exact address/height/index checks, rx-accepted status in the same state, one acceptance per index) against the manual's verify-output-proof script and Dave.

hash_tree.verify_slice does not check that sibling hashes are 32-byte strings; I argued it is still sound because the sibling count is fixed and every real inner node has a 64-byte preimage (a wrong-length sibling can only add, never remove, a level), so not reported. No fuzzing was done.

Ran a randomized differential test (600 trials, heights 1-10) of the Lua outputs frontier (frontier, push_back, append, get_root_hash, next_proofs, frontier-from-last-proof) against a naive padded tree with libcmt's zero pristine leaf: 0 mismatches. frontier_pad_back and the frontier_forest_* functions were not tested.

libcmt cmt_rollup_finish caches the root by leaf count (finish_leaf_count); a stale root would need cmt_rollup_reset_merkle/load_merkle to produce a different tree with the same count inside one process, which no shipped tool does; not reported. rollup-http-server's finish path was not read.

The PRT bridge's staging/acceptance job scheduling and transaction ordering (support), crisium multi-epoch checkpoint and outputs-root continuity were read only as far as the EpochSealed outputsMerkleRoot check (consistent).
Sentry fast-path settlement and the guardian/foreclosure interplay beyond what R1-A5-1 already covers; CartesiStateTransition and the step verifiers (other angles).
vg.lua (verification-game referee) output handling beyond confirming it shares game-output.lua.
